description: On the real paired branch, downgrading the contract migration to its own down_revision (the S1 expand revision id) then upgrade head recreates the schema: tracking_code is present nullable after the downgrade and absent after upgrade head (mark @pytest.mark.migration)
After downgrading the contract migration to its down_revision, tracking_code equals location-batch-serial for every row whose batch_number and serial_number are both non-NULL
After downgrading the contract migration to its down_revision, tracking_code is NULL for every row where batch_number or serial_number is NULL

After the contract downgrade then upgrade head round-trip, the test's own seeded stock_records rows are all still present with identical sku, location, quantity, batch_number and serial_number (delta scoped to per-run-unique keys)

After the contract upgrade, the test's own seeded stock_records rows, including NULL batch/serial rows, all exist with sku, location, quantity, batch_number and serial_number equal to the expand-revision snapshot
A forced failure inside the contract migration transaction leaves stock_records at the expand revision with tracking_code still present
A forced failure inside the contract migration transaction leaves every seeded stock_records row present and unchanged
After the contract migration, a direct INSERT duplicating an existing (sku, location) is rejected by the UNIQUE constraint
After the contract migration, a direct INSERT with quantity -1 is rejected by CHECK ck_stock_records_quantity_non_negative
After the contract migration, batch_number is still nullable: a direct INSERT with batch_number NULL succeeds
After the contract migration, serial_number is still nullable: a direct INSERT with serial_number NULL succeeds
The integration test session fixture asserts the engine dialect is postgresql and its URL is the paired branch DATABASE_URL, failing fast otherwise
